thesis: PayPal (Nasdaq: PYPL). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-27) downloaded and read in part (statements, MD&A key metrics, restructuring and litigation notes). Q3 revenue 8,584M vs 8,417M (+2.0%); 9M 25,619M vs 24,496M (+4.6%); TPV Q3 487.1B (+6%), 9M 1,437.5B (+9%); active accounts 440M (+1%); payment transactions +7%; Q3 operating income 1,402M vs 1,520M (-8%), operating margin 16% vs 18%; Q3 NI 1,073M vs 1,248M (-14%); diluted EPS 1.25 vs 1.30. Transaction revenue grew slower than TPV on mix, co-marketing incentives with large merchants and lower FX fees. TTM (FY25 10-K + 9M26 - 9M25, USD millions): NI 4,727 (5,233+3,290-3,796); OCF 7,093 (6,416+4,709-4,032); PP&E capex 794 (852+600-658); FCF 6,299; SBC 977 (1,002+767-792); FCF after SBC 5,322. Close 57.89 (2026-11-18) x 830,658,298 shares (10-Q cover, 2026-10-21) = 48.09B market cap = 10.2x TTM NI; FCF yield 13.1% (11.1% after SBC). Cash, short and long term investments 15,065M (upper bound, long term investments include non marketable equity) vs debt 13,472M (short term 2,533M, long term 10,939M; 4.550%, 4.950%, 5.550% senior notes issued May 2026): roughly net cash 1.6B, excluding 38.4B of customer funds. Buybacks 4,553M cash in 9M26 (about 9.5% of market cap annualized pace about 12.6%). Price implies earnings stay flat to slightly down; what differs: strong cash conversion and buybacks versus a market treating branded checkout growth as impaired (securities suits allege undisclosed impediments to branded checkout and the 2027 targets). Possible mispricing is cyclical or share loss; this record does not show which.
counterthesis: Operating income fell 8% in Q3 and 5% in 9M despite 6% TPV growth; transaction expense grows faster than revenue; restructuring charges 255M in Q3 (442M 9M) are recurring across 2025 and 2026 plans. OCF in 9M rose 17% but Q3 OCF fell 19% (1,592M vs 1,974M), and cash flow includes loan receivable and customer fund timing, so FCF yield of 13% may overstate owner earnings. 1.5B of Japan installment loans were moved to held for sale and consumer loans fell 19%, so credit exposure is changing. Active accounts grow 1%. Multiple legal matters: branded checkout securities class action, CFPB civil investigative demands on Regulation E and PayPal Credit, an EU proceeding, derivative suits (outcomes unread). Debt rose (long term 13.4B at 9/30 per XBRL tag vs 10.9B at March) while cash fell. Peers (Block, Adyen, Fiserv, Visa) and own multiple history not compared; MD&A margin drivers read only in part. Other income swung to -240M in 9M from +111M (cause unread).
invalidation: Invalidated if TPV growth falls below low single digits for two quarters with transaction margin dollars shrinking, if operating margin keeps falling below about 15%, if CFPB or securities matters bring a material penalty, or if cash flow shows the FCF is mostly working capital or customer fund timing.
